scope: Production BackendRuntime factory and SQLite with injected HTTP/native process port

checks.description: A ready manifest whose real API envelope exceeds the ceiling emits no bytes or exposure; a new SQLite/runtime instance accepts the later source under a larger ceiling and the same Session.
Operator admission refusal rolls back all API possible exposure; a later allowed request succeeds without an unresolved context barrier.
An outer backend-receipt insertion failure rolls back the inner API input/send records and request-start budget; the successor uses only committed intent identity.
A request that reaches the injected transport then loses confirmation retains unknown request/input/claim across recovery and blocks a successor; no uncertainty is cleared by the API admission fix.
The injected SDK port sees persisted possible exposure before accepting its local prompt, even with zero HTTP; lack of a terminal anchor forces the next native identity cold.
checks.limitation: An injected SDK process port is used; this does not claim a real native process or supplier.
